gloss: to show one's skill; to demonstrate one's ability; to display one's talents

definitions.gloss: to show one's skill; to demonstrate one's ability; to display one's talents
definitions.explanation: To actively demonstrate or exercise one's skills, especially in a situation where those abilities can be fully utilized. Often used when someone gets an opportunity to use their expertise.

examples.japanese: {料理|りょうり}の{腕|うで}を{振|ふ}るってもてなした。
examples.english: I showcased my cooking skills to entertain the guests.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{腕|うで}を{振|ふ}るう{機会|きかい}だ。
examples.english: Today is a chance to show what I can do.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しいプロジェクトで{思|おも}う{存分|ぞんぶん}{腕|うで}を{振|ふ}るいたい。
examples.english: I want to fully demonstrate my abilities in the new project.

notes:
IDIOM STRUCTURE:
{腕|うで} (arm; skill) + を + {振|ふ}るう (to wield; to exercise)

{腕|うで} here means skill/ability, not literally the arm. {振|ふ}るう means to wield or exercise something actively.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {料理|りょうり}の{腕|うで}を{振|ふ}るう - to show off cooking skills
- {腕|うで}を{振|ふ}るう{機会|きかい} - opportunity to show one's skill
- {腕|うで}を{振|ふ}るう{場|ば} - place to demonstrate ability
- {思|おも}う{存分|ぞんぶん}{腕|うで}を{振|ふ}るう - to fully exercise one's skills

USAGE:
Positive expression. Implies:
- Having genuine skill to demonstrate
- Having an appropriate opportunity
- Enthusiasm to show one's abilities
- Active engagement, not just passive display

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {腕|うで}を{見|み}せる - to show one's skill
- {実力|じつりょく}を{発揮|はっき}する - to demonstrate one's ability
- {手腕|しゅわん}を{発揮|はっき}する - to display one's capability
- {才能|さいのう}を{発揮|はっき}する - to show one's talent

RELATED WORDS:
{腕|うで}を{磨|みが}く - to hone one's skills (complementary - first you polish, then you show)
